rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Panopticon, The Prisoner, and the Crowd", "body": "Mike Winner opened the conversation with the panopticon, a circular prison design he described as keeping inmates in line through the chance of being watched, and he compared it to what he called a virtual panopticon today. Chance responded by recommending the 1960s series The Prisoner, which he described as an examination of the crowd versus the individual. Chance said he believed that resisting the crowd and holding fast eventually led people either to let the individual go or to ask that person to lead. He framed the conflict as the infinite divine spark exploring itself."}, {"title": "Evil Intent, Pop Gnosticism, and Sin", "body": "Mike noted that Chance had been vocal against pop Gnosticism and the idea of a prison planet. One host called the notion that God teaches through evil nonsense, and Chance answered that he believed bad actors exist but that all things serve good in the end. Chance said that when he asked proponents of the soul trap idea what freedom would mean, he heard that any remaining sense of I am meant still being trapped, which he took to imply a goal of obliteration. He also described sin as consequences that follow from acting against nature's order."}, {"title": "Polarized Energy and the Biofield", "body": "Chance described the biofield as a six foot bubble around the body and said he believed the polarized energy farthest from the body dated from the earliest years of life. He explained that his method of Biofield Tuning, which he said he learned from Eileen Day McKusick, aimed to help people see where they held that energy and what beliefs sat behind it. Chance said symptoms and injuries could be read as messages from the body. He also reframed anxiety as excitement, describing it as energy that could be used or left to stagnate."}, {"title": "Language as Technology and Hidden Names", "body": "Chance said the word technology originally meant language, and he described his own approach as the green language, reading words through both left brain and right brain meanings. Asked about a perennial source of traditions, he said he believed the common source was nature. He read a passage from Godfrey Higgins about the limits of human knowledge, and he argued that the Logos of many traditions symbolized the knowledge of alphabets. Chance also described euhemerism, in which he said a historical figure was reshaped to fit a savior doctrine, using Cyrus and Isaiah as an example."}, {"title": "Sound, Synchronicity, and Numbers", "body": "Barre Lando said sound was the creative mechanism, describing it through the alchemical idea of a water or sound ether, and he contrasted a deterministic simulation with the view, which he credited to Walter Russell, that people were co-creators. Barre then asked about synchronicity and numbers. Chance replied that the meaning of a number depended on a person's relationship to it, and he offered his view that certain values such as 600, 608, and 650 recurred in the names of savior deities. Chance closed by describing tuning as a consistent process and the throat as a key bottleneck."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined hosts Mike Winner and Barre Lando on AlfaCast for a live conversation that ranged from the panopticon and The Prisoner to language as a technology and my Biofield Tuning work.
